title: Architecture
description: The Architect Reviewer's structured output for a feature, persisted as features/<F>/architecture.json (the machine-checkable companion to architecture.md). NFRs live HERE, not on the spec-author-owned, spec-gated feature-spec.json/story.json: the architect proposes them and the HIL (Product Owner) accepts or modifies them at Gate 2. Moving NFRs off feature-spec.json resolves the spec-gate integrity drift: the architect annotating feature-spec.json after the spec gate hashed it tripped verify-gate-integrity.

service_backed.description: REQUIRED, explicit boolean (no silent omission): the architect must make a deliberate call. True when the feature persists data or carries business logic (anything beyond a trivial static/read-through endpoint); then it MUST declare layered `layers` (boundary+service+repository) and a layering fitness test, and checkLayeringDeclared/checkFitnessCoverage hard-block the gate. False ONLY for a trivial feature (the YAGNI guard). A false/absent declaration is cross-checked against evidence: checkServiceBackedDeclaration hard-blocks the gate when the feature shows persistence evidence (an Infra-layer AC, or an NFR about migrations/schema/storage), so under-declaration cannot silently disable layering enforcement.

layers.description: The module layering the build must realize (boundary -> service -> repository -> ORM, dependencies inward). Required in substance for a service_backed feature. The boundary never imports the DB session; persistence lives only in the repository; business logic only in the service.

module.description: Path/dotted-module this layer lives in (e.g. app/routes, app/services, app/repositories). For the `models` role declare a PACKAGE directory (app/models/, trailing slash), one module per domain object/aggregate, NOT a flat app/models.py; checkModulePlacement enforces the package shape and the architecture-conventions check keeps it consistent across features.

may_import.description: Layer roles this one is allowed to depend on (inward). Empty/omitted means it depends on nothing inward.

renders_via.description: Boundary layer only (UI features): the templating framework the boundary renders through (e.g. "jinja2" + a templates/ dir). The boundary returns a rendered template, never an inline HTML string; consort-layering-clean flags inline HTML with no templating seam. Omit for API/CLI/Infra boundaries that return data, not markup.

persistence_invariants.description: The DB-level guarantees the schema must enforce (the persistence contract), for a feature that persists data. This array is the source of truth for 'this feature has a database': a service does NOT always mean a database, so a service_backed compute/proxy/aggregator that persists nothing declares NONE here (and is then routed past the DBA + DB-integration tests). Each declared invariant is covered by a real-branch test (a test-list item referencing its id via invariant_id) and physically realized by the DBA; checkPersistenceCoverage/checkDbDesign hard-block Gate 3 when a feature that DID declare invariants leaves one uncovered/unrealized. The safety net against under-declaring a feature that really persists is checkServiceBackedDeclaration (persistence evidence , an Infra AC or a storage/migration NFR , forces invariants). These drive DB-integration coverage tied to the schema's own contract, verifying the MIGRATION realized each guarantee against the branch, NOT the ORM's generic behavior.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. "PI1-stock-sku-location-unique". Referenced by a test-list item's invariant_id.

type.description: The class of guarantee: a unique key, an FK, a cascade rule, a NOT NULL, a CHECK, a transactional-atomicity boundary, or migration up-then-down reversibility.

table.description: The table (and, in brief, columns) the invariant applies to. Omit for a purely transactional/migration invariant.

brief.description: One line: the guarantee to verify against the real branch (e.g. "inserting two rows with the same (sku, location) is rejected").

nfrs.description: Non-functional requirements proposed by the architect, adjudicated by the HIL at Gate 2. An empty array is valid (a feature may have no NFRs), but every entry that exists must be HIL-considered, not unconsidered. Each NFR states its requirement (via `brief`, or the legacy `requirement`) and, per @architectural-design-principles, NAMES the fitness function that defends it (`fitness_function`) so the Test Strategist authors it as a RED test.

id.description: Stable NFR id, e.g. "NFR-F1-durability-migrations". Read by the context rubric + downstream roles.

category.description: The NFR quality attribute, e.g. performance / scalability / security / observability / operability / resilience / durability / correctness / testability / usability / configurability. A free string (the quality-attribute set is open), not a fixed enum.

requirement.description: Legacy field for the requirement statement. Prefer `brief`. One of `brief`/`requirement` is required.

brief.description: One line stating the requirement (e.g. "existing rows survive every additive migration"). The field the context rubric + downstream roles read; one of `brief`/`requirement` is required.

fitness_function.description: The concrete, real-branch test that DEFENDS this NFR (e.g. "integration test applies the Alembic revision over seeded rows and asserts survival + clean down"). Per @architectural-design-principles every architectural constraint names the fitness function that defends it, recorded so the Test Strategist authors it as a RED test. Omit only for an NFR with no machine-checkable defense. Use this SINGULAR form ONLY for a single-obligation NFR; when the guarantee is multi-part, use `fitness_functions` (array) instead so each clause is defended by its own test.

fitness_functions.description: The ATOMIC per-clause form of `fitness_function`: ONE independently-testable obligation per entry. Use this INSTEAD of packing multiple checks into one `fitness_function` prose string (the compound form the reflect gate has to decompose, which it does inconsistently across laps and surfaces ONE-uncovered-clause-per-lap - the piecemeal reflect thrash). Each entry is defended by its OWN test; the Test Strategist authors one `fitness` test per entry, tagging each with this NFR's `id` via the test-list item's `nfr_id`, and the reflect gate checks coverage PER ENTRY deterministically (no prose decomposition). When present, `checkFitnessClauseCoverage` hard-blocks the test_list gate unless every entry is covered by a test referencing this NFR's `id`. Requires this NFR to set `id`. Mutually exclusive with `fitness_function` (set one or the other, never both).

applies_to.description: Feature or story id this NFR scopes to. Omit for feature-wide NFRs.

hil_status.description: Architect proposes; the HIL accepts/modifies/rejects at Gate 2.

brief_ref.description: The R<n> id of the nfrs.md Required item this NFR satisfies. Every Required item in the HIL's nfrs.md must be covered by some architecture.json nfr carrying its id here, or checkNfrCoverage hard-blocks the architecture gate. Omit for architect-originated NFRs that no Required item drove.

tier.description: How this NFR is defended. `product` (the default, and the behavior of any untiered NFR): feature-specific — threaded into every relevant story's rubric and defended by per-story fitness tests. `platform`: cross-cutting / substrate-guaranteed (layering, config-in-env, observability, auth-ready posture, operability) — defended ONCE, not per story, so it is NOT injected into the per-story rubric and needs no per-clause per-story test. A `platform` NFR must NAME its defense (it is never dropped): set `defended_by_gate` to the deterministic gate that enforces it, OR give it a single feature-level `fitness_function`. checkPlatformNfrDefended hard-blocks a `platform` NFR that has neither. It still carries `brief_ref`, so checkNfrCoverage traceability is preserved.

defended_by_gate.description: For a `tier:"platform"` NFR defended by an existing deterministic gate rather than a per-story fitness test — e.g. "consort-layering-clean" (inward-dependency layering + ORM-containment) or "config-in-env". Satisfies checkPlatformNfrDefended in lieu of a fitness_function. Ignored for product-tier NFRs.

open_decisions.description: Architectural decisions deliberately LEFT UNRESOLVED here (deferred boundary/design questions, e.g. whether a canonical SKU catalog table should exist vs. treating stock_records as the SKU authority). First-class so a LATER story cannot silently resolve one in a way that contradicts an earlier, already-gated story: the cross-story design review reads these, and a story that resolves an open decision must record how (decision_status -> "resolved", resolved_by_story, resolution) and reconcile it against the stories that deferred it. Empty is valid.

question.description: The unresolved decision, one line (e.g. "Is stock_records the authority on whether a SKU is 'known', or is a separate SKU catalog needed?").

decision_status.description: open = still unresolved; resolved = a later story settled it (set resolved_by_story + resolution); deferred = intentionally postponed to a named later story.

resolved_by_story.description: The story id that resolved this decision. Set together with decision_status=resolved.

resolution.description: How it was resolved, one line , the reconciliation the cross-story review checks siblings against.
